title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance (Canonical)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's canonical architecture and engineering standards across API design, coding style, infrastructure (IaC), model-serving, observability, and performance. The goal is to provide a single, operational reference that teams can follow to ensure consistency, reliability, and measurable SLOs across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope
- Applies to all backend services, public APIs, model-serving components, and platform-level infrastructure maintained by Engineering.
- Does not replace team-level implementation guides; it defines cross-cutting controls, toolchain choices, and mandatory guardrails.

Principles
- Developer ergonomics first: clear defaults, automated checks, and templates.
- Production-grade by default: every change must consider SLO impact and observability.
- Explicit contracts: API versioning and contract tests are mandatory for public APIs.
- Cost-aware performance: batching, caching and quantization recommendations must be tracked in PRs that affect inference.

1) API Standards
Intro
APIs are the primary integration surface for customers and internal services. Follow these rules for design, versioning, authentication, and testing.

Design & Naming
- Use REST+JSON for public control-plane APIs; use gRPC internally for high-throughput service-to-service paths.
- Resource-oriented endpoints: /v{major}/{resource}/{id}/subresource. Avoid RPC-style verbs in URL paths.
- Use nouns for resources and HTTP verbs for actions.

Versioning
- Major versions (breaking changes) -> URL versioning (/v1, /v2).
- Minor/patch -> backward compatible; indicate via response headers (X-Api-Version: 1.2.3).

Requests & Responses
- All JSON responses must include a top-level metadata block: {"request_id": string, "served_by": string, "api_version": string}.
- Use RFC3339 timestamps for any timestamps.

Authentication & Authorization
- Public APIs: bearer token (OAuth2 or Redwood API tokens).
- Internal services: mTLS + short-lived service tokens issued by the platform.

Rate Limiting & Quotas
- Implement per-token and per-route rate limiting via the API gateway. Default quotas: 100 req/s per token for write routes, 1000 req/s per token for read (subject to plan).

Contract Testing
- Every public API must include a contract test suite (Postman/Newman or Pact) stored alongside the service. Contract tests run in CI and gate merges to main for API-affecting changes.

Example: Minimal response payload
{
  "request_id": "req_0123456789",
  "served_by": "api-prod-1b",
  "api_version": "1.0.0",
  "data": { ... }
}

2) Coding Standards
Scope & Languages
- Primary backend languages: Go (core runtime, infra services), Python (data pipelines, evals), TypeScript (console/frontend).
- Use the company standard linter and formatter for each language (gofmt+golangci-lint, black+ruff, eslint+prettier).

Repository Structure
- One service per repo (microservice). Shared libraries live in dedicated monorepos with stable release tags.

PR & Review Checklist (required items)
1. Link to relevant design doc or ADR.
2. Tests: unit + integration where applicable.
3. Benchmark/perf changes included (if touching hot paths).
4. Security checklist: KMS usage, secrets handling.
5. Observability: metrics/span added for new latency or error surface.

Error Handling
- Prefer explicit errors with codes and structured context. Do not return opaque 500s. Use error codes mapped to API contract.

Testing
- Unit tests: target 80% for core libraries, 60% for services.
- Integration tests: CI runs ephemeral environments for any change touching infra or model-serving.

3) Infrastructure (IaC) Standards
IaC Tooling & Modules
- Terraform >= 1.4 for cloud resources. Use canonical modules under infra-modules repo.
- Cloud: AWS primary. Abstract cloud specifics via modules so Private deployments can swap implementations.

Networking & Security
- VPCs: default private subnets for compute, public subnets only for load balancers.
- Egress rules: deny-by-default, explicit allow lists.
- Secrets: store secrets in KMS-backed secret manager (AWS Secrets Manager or customer KMS for Private).

Tagging & Ownership
- All cloud resources must include tags: service, owner, cost_center, environment. Example: { service: 'inference-api', owner: 'team-inference', cost_center: 'INF-PLT', environment: 'prod' }

Change Control
- All infra changes must go through PR with plan output attached. Critical changes (network, VPC, KMS) require 48-hour review and review by infra owners.

4) Model-Serving Standards
Packaging & Model Artifacts
- Models must be packaged as immutable artifacts with metadata: model_id, model_version, architecture, tokenizer_version, quantization_profile. Store manifests in model-registry (git-backed).

Execution & Runtime Configs
- Recommended runtime resource profiles: small (4GB GPU share), medium (16GB), large (48-80GB) — documented per model family.
- Provide production configs for kernel selection and quantization policy per model: e.g., kernel: fused-attention-v2, quant: int8-llm-boost.

Caching & Batching
- Prefix/KV caching is mandatory for chat endpoints that expect repeated context tokens.
- Default batching windows: 2ms latency-first for low-latency routes; 10-30ms throughput-first for bulk inference. Document expected tail-latency impact in PRs.

Routing & Fallbacks
- Smart routing rules: prefer lowest-cost compatible variant that meets latency SLO. Canary->A/B rollout supported. Fallback chain must include at least two compatible variants (e.g., quantized and FP16).

Quality & Regression Controls
- Every model change that impacts generation must be accompanied by eval runs against the official prompt-set and a quality sign-off (QA or applied-ML reviewer).

5) Observability Standards
Goals
- Every service must be observable at token-level cost and latency granularity for inference paths and at request-level for control-plane APIs.

Metrics (minimum set)
- request.count, request.latency.p50/p90/p99, request.errors.count (by code), tokens.generated.count, model.kv.cache.hit_rate, batch.size.avg.
- Metric units and labels: labels must include service, route, model_id, model_version, region.

Tracing
- Use OpenTelemetry for traces. Traces must include spans for: auth, routing, model-inference, batching, cache lookup. Propagate request_id.

Logs
- Structured JSON logs with keys: ts, level, service, request_id, msg, error. No plaintext secrets in logs.

Dashboards & Alerts
- Per-route dashboard (latency, errors, throughput, cost).
- Pager alerting: SLO burn rate > 2x for 15m or error rate increase > 5% absolute for 5m.

Example Metric Tagging Table
| metric | required labels | frequency |
| request.latency.p99 | service, route, region, model_id | 10s |
| tokens.generated.count | service, model_id, model_version | 60s |

6) Performance Standards & Benchmarks
SLOs (example baselines)
- Control-plane read APIs: p95 latency < 120ms, availability 99.95%.
- Inference (chat, hosted): p95 token latency < 150ms on production flavor, throughput 500 tokens/s per GPU (model dependent).
- Batch/throughput jobs: job success within SLA of 99.5% for scheduled bulk jobs.

Benchmarking Process
1. Define workload (op distribution, sequence lengths, concurrency).
2. Use canonical perf-suite (see eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite) to run repeatable tests.
3. Record environment, kernel selections, and quantization profile.
4. Store results in the perf-dashboard and link from PR.

Load Testing & Capacity Planning
- Run load tests against canary stacks. Avoid testing on prod unless authorized and isolated.
- SRE owns capacity model; teams update capacity forecasts quarterly or when usage growth > 15% month-over-month.

7) ADRs (Decision Records)
Format & Storage
- ADRs follow the template: Title, Date, Status (accepted/rejected), Context, Decision, Consequences, Owners. Store ADRs under confluence/architecture-and-standards and mirror in the repo's docs/adr directory.

Recent ADRs
- ADR-2025-11: default-quantization-policy
  - Date: 2025-11-12
  - Status: accepted
  - Decision: Adopt int8-llm-boost as the default quantization profile for non-sensitive workloads; provide FP16 fallback for latency-critical routes.
  - Owners: Priya Rao, Marco Chen

- ADR-2026-01: runtime-kernel-selection
  - Date: 2026-01-22
  - Status: accepted
  - Decision: Runtime will use dynamic kernel selector that prioritizes fused kernels when sequence length <= 2048, otherwise use block-sparse kernels.
  - Owners: Evan Brooks, Aisha Patel

- ADR-2026-02: api-versioning-strategy
  - Date: 2026-02-10
  - Status: accepted
  - Decision: External API uses URL major-versioning; internal APIs may use header versions.
  - Owners: Sasha Ivanov

8) Release & Rollout Playbook (short)
Pre-release (PR stage)
1. Attach design doc/ADR link and perf results.
2. Run unit + integration + contract tests.
3. Run model evals for any model-impacting change.
4. Obtain sign-off from Observability and Security owners for infra-impacting changes.

Canary/Deploy
1. Deploy to canary with 5% traffic. Monitor key metrics for 30 minutes.
2. If canary passes (no SLO regression, no alerts), progress to 25% for 1 hour.
3. Full rollout in doubling steps (25% -> 50% -> 100%) with metrics validation at each step.
4. Automated rollback if p99 latency increases > 50ms or error rate increases > 2% absolute for 10 minutes.

Post-release
- Create release note with linked perf data, ADRs, and rollout timeline. Schedule a 1-week post-deploy review if the change touched model-serving or infra.

9) Incident Response & Postmortem Expectations
- Incidents affecting SLOs: open incident on PagerDuty, attach runbook, and notify customer-success for external impact.
- Postmortem: publish within 7 days with timeline, root cause, corrective actions, and owner for each action.

Appendix: Examples & Snippets
1) Example API curl
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"Hello", "max_tokens":64}'

2) Minimal Terraform tag module usage (example)
# main.tf
module "redwood_tags" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/infra-modules.git//tags?ref=v1.2.0"
  service = "inference-api"
  owner = "team-inference"
  cost_center = "INF-PLT"
  environment = "prod"
}

3) Example ADR template (use as file: docs/adr/000-template.md)
Title: [short title]
Date: YYYY-MM-DD
Status: proposed | accepted | deprecated
Context:
Decision:
Consequences:
Owners:
